A1.justification: Despite the TACO-to-LATTE renaming, both PDFs describe the same research pipeline, models, and core dataset. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching implementation and prompt listings.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations across eight benchmarks, data-mixture and hyperparameter ablations, and qualitative analyses, including additional appendix results.

after.justification: v3 retains original evaluations and adds distillation and agent comparisons, training-size experiments, an inference-format control, and quantitative error analysis.

M1.justification: LATTE retains TACO's thought-action-observation procedure, 15 tools plus Terminate, loss on thoughts and actions, and model-based and programmatic data generation with filtering. The appendix implementations and prompts are substantively unchanged. Renaming CoTA to LATTE-trace and emphasizing vision specialists do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds CV-Bench evaluation and uses additional baseline training corpora, including Visual-CoT. Coverage remains focused on visual question answering. A-OKVQA, MMMU, and MMVP disappear from the main comparison but remain in appendix experiments; both dataset-statistics tables retain the same 293,105 examples across 31 sources.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated comparisons with VPD and LLaVA-CoT in Table 2 and LLaVA-Plus and CogCoM in Table 3. Appendix B.3 also adds Visual-CoT results, although Table 8 labels its other row VPD-LLaVA despite prose describing a LATTE comparison. v1's GPT-4o and unfine-tuned prompting comparison in Table 1 is removed.

E3.justification: v3 introduces matched 98K-example baseline comparisons, training-size experiments at 98K/200K/293K, and a mixed LATTE/Direct training control tested with two inference formats. Main reporting changes from an eight-benchmark average to six benchmarks grouped by perception and reasoning. The LLaVA-OV Stage 1 configuration is dropped; core training and judging settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test training-data scaling, inference-time use of reasoning traces, and comparative perceptual failures on BLINK. Table 6 adds a quantitative MMVet error taxonomy. Existing data-format, source, programmatic-mixture, and hyperparameter ablations are largely retained or reorganized, with the hyperparameter and programmatic examples moved to the appendix.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for benchmark performance. v3's error-category percentages add descriptive analysis rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial benchmark and analysis results: Table 2 reports 98K-example overall scores of 45.2 for LATTE versus 40.4 for both VPD and LLaVA-CoT. Retained configurations also have revised scores, including Mantis-SigLIP instruction-tuned MMVet changing from 45.7 to 50.0 without an explained setting change. The new six-benchmark averages cannot be directly compared with v1's eight-benchmark averages.

T1.justification: Equations 1–2 retain the same sequence and thought-action-observation definitions, with the sequence renamed from C to T. Neither version adds theoretical guarantees, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: v3 reframes the contribution around offloading perception to vision specialists so small models can concentrate on reasoning. It adds claims of superiority over distillation methods and explicitly positions the dataset as the largest collection of its kind. This substantially changes the scope of the original action-model and direct-answer-baseline claims.

C2.justification: v3 identifies weak perception as the primary bottleneck and interprets distillation failures and fallback to the model's own perception through that explanation. It adds an observation that mixed-format training produces Direct responses around 70% of the time, plus error-based recommendations for tool diversity. Limitations now discuss supervised-finetuning generalization and possible reinforcement-learning alternatives.

D1.justification: v3 explains its VPD reproduction by converting LATTE traces to CoT format and documents filtering Visual-CoT to 413K examples with valid bounding boxes. Appendix H adds artifact licensing and Llama license information. Existing implementation listings, prompts, dataset statistics, and core hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The extensive language-only tool-use survey is removed, and positioning shifts toward perception specialists and reasoning distillation. v3 adds LLaVA-CoT and supporting perception, neuroscience, and test-time-compute references. New Appendix A/Table 7 compares competing datasets and models to support expanded scale and multimodal-trace novelty claims.

P1.justification: The title, terminology, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work moves from Section 4 to Section 2, experiments are reorganized around two research questions and error analysis, and limitations receive a separate section. The appendix structure is also substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: v3 adds an overview diagram, scaling plots, comparison tables, and an error table. Main results are redesigned around perception/reasoning groups, while data-format ablations change from detailed table rows to grouped bars. Existing qualitative and hyperparameter figures are relocated or resized, and the document is extensively reformatted.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's lack of evaluated peer-method comparisons through matched-budget distillation experiments, adds an inference-format control, and quantifies failure modes. These strengthen the empirical support and understanding of the approach. The gains outweigh new reporting problems, including the abstract's 273K versus the body's 293K dataset size and ambiguous Table 8 labeling. Higher headline gains over a changed benchmark set do not themselves establish improvement.
